quotes.text: “Ask not what your country can do for you — ask what you can do for your country.”

quotes.text: “Two roads diverged in a wood, and I— / I took the one less traveled by, / And that has made all the difference.”
quotes.attribution: Robert Frost, “The Road Not Taken,” Mountain Interval (1916); text per Poetry Foundation

quotes.text: “They shall grow not old, as we that are left grow old: / Age shall not weary them, nor the years condemn.”
quotes.attribution: Laurence Binyon, “For the Fallen” (first published in The Times, Sept. 21, 1914)

quotes.text: “To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.”

quotes.text: My subject is War, and the pity of War. The Poetry is in the pity.
quotes.attribution: Wilfred Owen, draft preface to Poems (written 1918, published 1920)

quotes.text: May we never see another War! for in my Opinion there never was a good War, or a bad Peace.
